facts.fact: Growth hacking is defined on the page as the use of resource-light and cost-effective marketing tactics to help grow and retain an active user base, sell products and gain exposure.
facts.quote: Growth hacking is the use of resource-light and cost-effective marketing tactics to help grow and retain an active user base, sell products and gain exposure.

facts.fact: The page states that growth hacking is most commonly associated with start-ups and small businesses, which lack large cash reserves but need quick results.
facts.quote: Growth hacking is most commonly associated with start-ups and small businesses, i.e., those organizations that don’t have a huge amount of cash to spare but need results quickly.

facts.fact: The page attributes the term 'growth hacker' to Sean Ellis, founder and chief executive of GrowthHackers.com.
facts.quote: This term was first coined by Sean Ellis, founder and current chief executive of GrowthHackers.com

facts.fact: The page states that Sean Ellis, who coined the term, was head of growth at Dropbox.com.
facts.quote: who, among a wealth of other positions, was head of growth at Dropbox.com.

facts.fact: In a 2010 blog post, Sean Ellis wrote that a growth hacker is a person whose true north is growth.
facts.quote: A growth hacker is a person whose true north is growth. Everything they do is scrutinized by its potential impact on scalable growth...

facts.fact: The page says growth hacks are often developed and implemented by a single person on the product or engineering team, without needing an entire marketing team.
facts.quote: Growth hacks are often developed and implemented by a single person on the product or engineering team, and don't require an entire marketing team to execute.

facts.fact: The page states that in 2024, growth hacking had become more sophisticated, incorporating AI-driven personalization, voice search optimization, blockchain, AR experiences and sustainability-focused growth.

facts.fact: The page cites Zoom as an example of growth hacking through a freemium model with limited meeting durations that drives upgrades.
facts.quote: Zoom: Freemium model with limited meeting durations, driving upgrades
